title: AI GTM & Growth Engineer
description:
6-month internship: agents, TypeScript & outbound. Hybrid, starting December 2026 to February 2027.


At a glance

  • Term: 6 months, starting between December 2026 and February 2027

  • Location: Marseille, France (coworking with a sea view, hybrid)

  • Stack: TypeScript · Next.js · React · Python · SQL · LLM APIs · PostgreSQL · BigQuery · Node.js · Pipedrive API · PostHog · AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex)

About Influentials

Influentials is a creator marketing platform and managed service built to help brands scale creator content. More than 16,000 creators are directly connected and verified on our platform, and more than 500 brands, including McDonald's, Disney, Samsung, ALDI and Volvo, have run over 5,000 campaigns with us. We're headquartered in Rotterdam, Netherlands and building our tech hub in Marseille, France.

How we build

AI is both how we build and what we build. We practise agentic engineering on a modern TypeScript stack: AI agents write most of the code, and humans specify and review everything that goes live. We merge hundreds of PRs each month, and our velocity keeps accelerating. We're not tied to one tool (Claude Code today, Codex before), and we adopt new practices as they land, like cloud coding agents and agent loops. The job is changing fast right now, and you'll learn it with us.

Our next step is international: the UK, Scandinavia and France. We're looking for a GTM & growth engineer intern to build the machine that gets us there.

Go-to-market as engineering

We treat GTM as a systems problem, not a creative writing exercise: pipelines, enrichment, sequencing, attribution. It's the same technical work as any full-stack engineer, backend and frontend, applied to growth instead of product features: pipelines and APIs, tools for our team, and small full-stack apps that brands use. You'll sit between sales, marketing and engineering, write TypeScript, Python and SQL, build AI agents that run in production, and measure what they bring. No-code is fine for a quick test; anything that lasts is built in code. This is AI engineering, not machine learning: agents, tools, prompts and evals built on top of existing LLMs. No model training.

What you'll build

This is an internship: you're here to learn, working alongside the CTO and the sales team. These are the projects you'll contribute to:

01. Free tools that bring brands to us. Small free apps on our website, built on our creator data and LLMs. You'll build them and measure how many brands they bring to the platform.

02. An AI agent that spots brands doing influencer marketing. Build an agent that analyses social media content (our creators' posts, captions and hashtags) to detect sponsored content and the brands behind it, then scrapes those brands' websites to enrich them. That's an intent signal: score these brands so the sales team calls the right ones first.

03. Pages built from our data. Public research pages generated from our creator data, that brands find on Google and in AI assistants.

04. Outbound sequences. Email sequences to brands, personalised with our creator data and research done by AI agents, A/B tested against clear conversion targets.

05. The creator acquisition engine. Our system finds creators and contacts them by email. Add AI analysis of their content to target the right creators, and improve deliverability and conversion.

06. CRM and attribution, from first contact to invoice. Leads pushed to Pipedrive in one click, deal stages in sync, and dashboards that show which source brings which revenue.

You won't do all six. With the CTO, you'll pick one, ship it, measure it, then move to the next.

Technical challenges

  • AI agents you can trust: evals on real social content to measure what the LLM gets right, and keeping cost and latency under control.

  • APIs in the real world: rate limits, retries, webhooks.

  • Deliverability: SPF, DKIM, DMARC, domain warm-up, bounces.

  • Data pipelines: from GTM tools (CRM, email, enrichment) to BigQuery, without losing data quality.

  • Experiments: A/B tests that are statistically sound, not "it felt better".

What success looks like

  • Month 1: you've learned the stack and the data, your first change is in production, and you've picked your first project with the CTO.

  • Months 2–3: your first project is live and measured.

  • Months 4–6: a second project, plus a weekly GTM dashboard the team actually reads, documented so it keeps running after you leave.

Who you'll work with

You'll work directly with Matthieu, our CTO, who cares as much about business and product as about code, and with our sales and partnerships leads. The rest of the team is in Rotterdam: weekly video calls with sales, campaign management and product, in English, with no travel needed. You'll be one of the first people in our Marseille tech hub, with a real scope and someone next to you to help you get there.


You might be a fit if

  • You're a final-year student looking for a 6-month internship (end-of-studies, or abroad as part of your degree). Engineering school, computer science, business informatics or a business/tech dual degree: your degree matters less than what you've built.

  • You already write code: TypeScript or Python, APIs, SQL, and you've built something with an LLM. You can judge what an AI wrote, and fix it when it's wrong.

  • You're scrappy: you'd rather ship a rough version on Monday than a perfect one in a month. You try things, build, measure, and keep what works.

  • You think in systems: you'd rather automate a task than do it twice, and you've used tools like Clay, Apollo or n8n enough to know when to replace them with code.

  • You care about quality, even for internal tools. You're as comfortable in a terminal as in a meeting with the sales team, and you can teach what you build.

  • You're comfortable working in English (weekly calls with the Rotterdam team). Day to day in Marseille, we speak French or English, whichever you prefer.

Nice to have: a side project that shows your tech curiosity: a mobile app, a small AI or web3 project, a scraper or data pipeline, ideally with real users.

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway.

Practical details

  • 6 months, starting between December 2026 and February 2027, with an internship agreement (convention de stage).

  • A coworking space in Marseille with a sea view. Flexible hybrid, around 2 remote days a week: we care about what you ship, not the hours you spend at your desk.

  • Students from other EU countries welcome, including Erasmus+ traineeships.

How we hire

  • A 15-minute call with Matthieu, our CTO, to get to know each other.

  • A 30-minute technical interview.


How to apply

Apply here with your CV and tell us about something you built or automated. Add a link to code you wrote if you can (a GitHub repo, a script, a pipeline, a side project); if your best work is private, just tell us about it. No cover letter needed.

P.S. If you've read this far, tell us in your application which of the six projects you'd start with, and why.

title: (Senior) Engineer, Equipment Engineering
description:
Step into a career with ASM, where cutting edge technology meets collaborative culture. ​

For over 55 years ASM has been ahead of what’s next, at the forefront of innovation and what’s technologically possible. With more than 4,500 ASMers representing 70 nationalities, our people and our advanced semiconductor devices are playing a crucial role in trends such as 5G, cloud computing, AI, and autonomous driving. But we’re more than just a tech company. We value diversity, inclusion and sustainability as we strive to make a positive impact on the world. Our development programs help support your growth, shaping your future and pushing the boundaries of innovation to unleash potential.

As a (Senior Engineer), Equipment Engineering at ASM, you will support the development, installation, and stable operation of advanced R&D equipment in new product development.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline

  • Basic understanding of wafer fab operations, gas and vacuum systems, and equipment control concepts
  • Familiarity with cleanroom or laboratory environments and safe handling of chemicals, gases, or related systems
  • Ability to communicate effectively in English and work collaboratively across engineering teams

What sets you apart

  • Experience with deposition equipment such as PEALD, PECVD, or similar thin-film tools
  • Expertise to RF-induced plasma systems, electro-pneumatic controls, robotics, or microprocessor-based controllers

title: Committee member
description:
- **Closing:**

   5:00pm, 20th Nov 2026 GMT



**About us**

Oak National Academy is an independent public body, funded by the Department for Education (DfE). We help teachers teach a high-quality curriculum and cut the time they spend planning lessons. Teachers across England use our free, fully sequenced, teacher-made resources, aligned to the national curriculum. We also build AI tools for teachers, including Aila, our AI lesson assistant.

Our mission is to improve pupil outcomes and close the disadvantage gap by supporting teachers to teach and enabling pupils to access a high-quality curriculum.

**Why join us**

This is a rare chance to gain committee experience in a national public body that's still small enough for your contribution to shape what it does. You'll:

- see how a lean EdTech organisation works at national scale, from curriculum design to product and AI decisions

- learn first-hand how government and the DfE sponsor, fund and hold a public body to account

- work alongside experienced leaders from education, technology and public governance

- build governance experience that sets you up for future board and trustee roles

- see your expertise shape resources used in classrooms every day


This could be your first committee role. If you bring the expertise, we'll help you build the governance experience.

**Our committees**

Our committees support the Board in carrying out its functions. They make sure governance and compliance arrangements work well, give strategic support and challenge, and monitor results and impact. They're an essential part of how we achieve our strategic aims.

- **Finance, Audit and Risk Committee:** oversees our financial management, risk control and internal audit, and makes sure we follow public sector financial rules and value-for-money principles.

- **Remuneration and HR Committee:** oversees our pay and benefits, making sure our remuneration policies are transparent, fair and in line with public sector guidelines.

- **Curriculum Committee:** makes sure our curriculum and resources improve educational outcomes and help close the disadvantage gap.

- **Product Committee:** oversees the strategy, development and delivery of our digital products, making sure our platforms and resources are innovative, user-focused and aligned with our mission.


**Responsibilities**

- Attend and actively contribute to at least three virtual committee meetings a year, providing informed input based on your area of expertise.

- Work effectively with other committee members to support the team to deliver against our strategic goals.

- Monitor performance against agreed targets and provide support, advice and challenge to the executive team on their delivery.

- Ensure committees operate within the limits of their authority, in accordance with the Nolan Principles and the Code of Conduct for Board Members of Public Bodies, and abide by the conditions relating to the use of public funds. This includes being seen as politically impartial and considering conflicts of interest.

- Ensure high standards of corporate governance are observed at all times and that we remain compliant with our statutory, legal and regulatory obligations.


**Knowledge, skills and experience**

You'll ideally have a proven track record in at least one of these areas:

- evidence-based curriculum and/or pedagogy

- teaching or school leadership

- special educational needs and disabilities (SEND)

- digital, technology or AI

- people, HR and culture

- commercial

- legal

- executive leadership


You'll also bring:

- the ability to make strategic, evidence-based decisions by drawing on and applying the latest information or research

- exceptional communication skills to build effective relationships at senior level and between organisations

- the ability to drive forward the work of an organisation at non-executive level, with a successful track record in the public, voluntary or private sector of ensuring strategic objectives are achieved

- demonstrated commitment to the values of public service, including the ethical use of public funds

- experience and knowledge that will contribute to the functioning of a committee


Above all, we're looking for good judgement on governance, risk and statutory compliance, a clear eye on performance, and the diligence and integrity that public service asks of all of us.

**Where we'd especially value your expertise**

Our current gaps are SEND and people and culture, so we'd especially like to hear from you if you bring either. We still want to hear from everyone with relevant expertise. We'll be recruiting to our Board with the DfE soon, and other opportunities will come up. With your permission, we'll keep your details on file and get in touch when they do.

**How to apply**

Upload your CV and a letter of interest. In your letter, tell us about the expertise you'd bring, which committee interests you, and whether you'd like us to consider you for future Board or committee roles.

- **Closing date:** Friday 20 November 2026

- **Interviews:** late November through to mid-December 2026

- **Appointments confirmed:** by the end of January 2027, subject to Secretary of State approval


We welcome applicants from every background. Our committees need to reflect the society we serve.

title: Vi søker Sykepleier til Sone Solvang
description:
Er du vår nye sykepleier på Sone Solvang?

En av våre kollegaer søker nye utfordringer, og vi søker derfor etter hennes erstatter i 100 % sykepleierstilling

Vi har også ledig 100% vikariat som sykepleier i perioden 01.03.2027 - 31.08.2028

Er du en sykepleier som ser muligheter i fremtidens helsevesen og ønsker en variert og meningsfull arbeidshverdag? Vi i hjemmetjenesten Sone Solvang søker en ny kollega til vårt team. Midt i sentrum av den flotte sommerbyen Tønsberg kan du nå få en spennende arbeidshverdag hvor du møter brukere med ulike behov og får brukt hele bredden av sykepleiefaget. Arbeidsdagene består hovedsakelig av planlagte oppdrag og faste besøk, men i hjemmesykepleien må man også være forberedt på det uforutsette og akutte som kan oppstå. Vi søker derfor deg som evner å omstille deg raskt, beholde roen og finne gode løsninger når situasjonen krever det.

Hva skal til for å trives hos oss?

Hos oss i Sone Solvang har vi spennende og innholdsrike dager med høyt tempo og stor variasjon. Vi har et godt arbeidsmiljø med mye humor og høy grad av psykologisk trygghet.

Ingen dager er like i hjemmesykepleien, og vi søker deg som trives med omstillinger og liker å finne gode løsninger sammen med andre. Vi er en positiv og faglig sterk gjeng som jobber tett sammen mot felles mål – å gi trygge, gode og fremtidsrettede tjenester til våre brukere. Vi er stolte av det gode arbeidsmiljøet vårt, hvor samarbeid, faglighet og humor står sterkt, og hvor kollegaer stiller opp for hverandre i hverdagen.

Hvem ser vi etter?

Vi ønsker oss en engasjert sykepleier som ønsker å bidra til gode og trygge tjenester for våre brukere. Hos oss er vi langt fremme i skoen og jobber aktivt med å se hvordan velferdsteknologi og digitale løsninger kan bidra til å avlaste tjenesten og gi brukerne større trygghet og mestring i eget hjem. Samtidig har vi et stort fokus på HMS og på å skape en trygg og bærekraftig arbeidshverdag for våre ansatte.

Du trives med å arbeide selvstendig ute hos brukerne, samtidig som du kjenner verdien av godt samarbeid og kollegastøtte. Hos oss står du aldri alene – vi hjelper hverandre og deler kunnskap og erfaringer i hverdagen.

Vi følger opp brukere i ulike aldre og livssituasjoner, og arbeidsoppgavene er både varierte og faglig utfordrende. Vi utfører blant annet ulike sykepleierprosedyrer i hjemmet, legemiddelhåndtering, sårbehandling, oppfølging av enteral og parenteral ernæring, hjemmedød, personlig stell og bruk av velferdsteknologiske løsninger.

Vi har faste rapporter, faglige møtepunkter og personalmøter med fokus på utvikling, kvalitet og kompetanseheving.

Det bes oppgitt i søknaden om man søker på fast stilling, vikariat, eller om begge stillinger er aktuelle. Kandidater vil bli kalt inn til intervju fortløpende i rekrutteringsfasen.

Hovedarbeidsoppgaver

  • Utføre helhetlig sykepleie til hjemmeboende brukere
  • Kartlegging, observasjon og oppfølging av brukeres helsetilstand
  • Sårbehandling
  • Sykepleieprosedyrer
  • Medikamenthåndtering
  • Ernæringsoppfølging (TPN, parenteral ernæring)
  • Samarbeid med fastleger, sykehus, tverrfaglige team, pårørende og andre samarbeidspartnere
  • Veiledning og støtte av ansatte, elever og studenter
  • Delta i utvikling av tjenesten og kvalitetsarbeid, med særlig fokus å HMS og pasientsikkerhet
  • Oppfølging av kroniske og akutte tilstander
  • Dokumentasjon i EPJ

Kvalifikasjoner

  • Norsk autorisasjon som sykepleier
  • Førerkort klasse B er et absolutt krav
  • Gode digitale ferdigheter
  • Gode norskkunnskaper, minimum nivå B2

Ønskede kvalifikasjoner

  • Ønskelig med erfaring eller interesse innen geriatri, demens eller helseteknologi
  • Ønskelig med erfaring fra lignende arbeid

Personlige egenskaper

Vi ser etter deg som er:

  • Fremtidsrettet og positiv til utvikling av fremtidens helse- og omsorgstjenester
  • Strukturert og opptatt av kvalitet og god dokumentasjon
  • Komfortabel med digitale verktøy og teknologi
  • Selvstendig, samtidig som du er en god lagspiller
  • Fleksibel og løsningsorientert i møte med ulike utfordringer

Nyutdannede sykepleiere eller sykepleiere som er ferdige i juni 2027 oppfordres til å søke. Personlig egnethet vil bli tillagt stor vekt.

Vi tilbyr

  • En spennende og variert arbeidshverdag, med faglige utfordringer.
  • Mulighet til å være med på utviklingen av fremtidens hjemmetjeneste
  • Et godt arbeidsmiljø med dyktige og støttende kollegaer
  • Årsturnus med mulighet til å påvirke egen arbeidsplan
  • 2- delt turnus, med hver tredje helg normalvakter, alternativt hver 4 helg langvakter (aktuelle stillinger er planlagt med hver 3 helg i 2027)
  • En tilgjengelig leder med fokus på arbeidsglede, mestring og HMS
  • Gode muligheter for faglig utvikling
  • Gode pensjons- og forsikringsordninger
  • Lønn etter gjeldende avtaleverk, startlønn tilsvarende nivå for 8 års ansiennitet.
  • Rekrutteringstillegg på 15 000 kr for lang erfaring (over 16 år)
  • Kompensasjon ved veilederansvar for studenter

Søkerlister med opplysninger om navn, alder, stilling eller yrkestittel og bosted- eller arbeidskommune for hver søker er offentlig i hht Offentlighetsloven. Det kan gjøres unntak dersom søker anmoder om dette og grunngir dette i søknaden. Dersom anmodningen ikke tas til følge vil søkeren varsles om dette.

Kommunen ber aldri om kontaktinformasjon eller kontoopplysninger i rekrutteringsfasen, verken over SMS, e-post eller i brev via Digipost

title: Doradca klienta UNIQA (Lublin)
description:
Wynagrodzenie
B2B: 5000 – 15000 PLN / mies. netto

Od 30 lat w Polsce tworzymy wyjątkowe miejsce pracy UNIQA. Jesteśmy jednym z liderów co do wielkości grup ubezpieczeniowych w Polsce. Chcemy, aby klienci wybierający UNIQA, wybierali lepsze życie. Zapewniamy im to, ubezpieczając i otaczając opieką ich zdrowie, życie i majątek. Co więcej, chcemy inspirować klientów do lepszego życia - dłuższego, zdrowszego i bezpieczniejszego. Z tą samą troską myślimy o naszych pracownikach.

Co możesz zyskać pracując z nami?

  • Fantastyczny zespół: Chcemy tworzyć różnorodne miejsce pracy i nie odrzucimy Twojej kandydatury ze względu na wiek, płeć czy pochodzenie. Współpracujemy zarówno z młodymi absolwentami jak i dojrzałymi pracownikami po 50 roku życia,

  • Świetne zarobki: Wynagrodzenie zależy od Twoich wyników. W tym zawodzie możesz zdecydować ile będziesz zarabiać dzięki określonym planom sprzedażowym, a w pierwszych dwóch latach współpracy, otrzymujesz premię wdrożeniową. Im dłużej pracujesz, tym wyższy Twój dochód pasywny,

  • Elastyczność: Wiemy, jak ważna jest równowaga między pracą a życiem prywatnym, dlatego do Twojej decyzji zostawiamy określenie czasu pracy. Dlatego ważna będzie Twoja dyscyplina i dobra organizacja zadań,

  • Rozwój: Zapewniamy szkolenia od podstaw. Jeśli wcześniej nie pracowałeś w ubezpieczeniach, nauczymy Cię wszystkich ważnych zagadnień oraz pokażemy jak rozmawiać z klientem, by stać się jego prawdziwym doradcą. Wielu naszych menedżerów zaczynało właśnie z nami, stawiając swoje pierwsze kroki na ścieżce kariery zawodowej,

  • Benefity: Ubezpieczenie grupowe, karta Medicover Sport, prywatna opieka medyczna.

Jakie zadania na Ciebie czekają?

  • Budowanie relacji: Pozyskujemy klientów z którymi chcemy budować zaufanie. Dać poczucie, że jesteśmy w stanie pomóc i wyjaśnić zawiłości świata ubezpieczeń, tłumacząc je na prostszy język,

  • Prezentacja oferty: Uważnie słuchamy naszych klientów, a następnie dopasowujemy produkty do ich potrzeb. Codziennie tworzymy rozwiązania, które przynoszą bezpieczeństwo. Chcemy być autentyczni i reagować na to co się dzieje w społeczeństwie, dlatego jako pierwsi w Polsce stworzyliśmy ochronę przed hejtem w Internecie,

  • Realizacja celów: Wraz z menedżerem ustalasz plany sprzedażowe, które będziesz realizował przez określony okres czasowy. Motywacja i konsekwencja zagrają tu główne skrzypce,

  • Szkolenia: Udział w szkoleniach produktowych i kompetencyjnych. Chcemy, by nasza kadra była na bieżąco ze zmianami oraz nowinkami rynku, nad czym pracujemy z profesjonalnymi trenerami.

Czego potrzebujesz do współpracy?

  • Wykształcenie min. średnie, co jest koniecznością,

  • Gotowość do współpracy w oparciu o własną działalność gospodarczą. Jeśli jej nie masz i założenie firmy wydaje się czarną magią, podpowiemy jak to zrobić,

  • Umiejętności interpersonalne: komunikacja, zdolność uważnego słuchania, empatia – to klucz do tej roli,

  • Chęć działania: Inicjatywa i dążenie do osiągania celów również będą bardzo istotne,

  • Zdolności organizacyjne: Jeśli potrafisz rozplanować efektywnie swój dzień oraz zarządzać sobą w czasie, to odnajdziesz się bez problemu.

Brzmi interesująco?

Dołącz do nas!

  • Wyślij swoje CV.

  • Spotkaj się z nami i lepiej się poznajmy.

  • Porozmawiamy o Twoich miękkich kompetencjach.

  • Przedstawimy Ci ofertę współpracy.

title: Business Director
description:
Business Director
Value Media | Warszawa I Praca hybrydowa

Do Value Media szukamy Business Directora, który będzie strategicznym partnerem dla naszych klientów i liderem zespołu odpowiedzialnego za ich biznes. W naszej agencji kierujemy się filozofią Data-Powered, Curiosity-Driven, która najlepiej opisuje nie tylko to, jak pracujemy dla klientów, ale też jakich ludzi chcemy mieć na pokładzie.

O roli:

To rola dla osoby, która potrafi patrzeć szerzej niż przez pryzmat pojedynczej kampanii marketingowej czy kanału mediowego. Rozumie biznes klienta, potrafi połączyć strategię, media, dane i technologię, a następnie zorganizować pracę zespołu ekspertów wokół wspólnego celu.

Nie szukamy osoby, która zna odpowiedzi na wszystkie pytania. Szukamy kogoś, kto potrafi zadawać właściwe pytania, wyciągać wnioski z danych i przekładać je na decyzje.

Będziesz pracować bezpośrednio z zespołami po stronie klienta: od CMO, CFO, CTO, procurement po zarząd – rozumiejąc ich cele, wyzwania i kontekst biznesowy.

Jednocześnie będziesz liderem/liderką zespołu po stronie agencji. Nie wymagamy ekspertyzy w każdym medium. Twoją rolą jest łączyć perspektywy, nadawać kierunek, podejmować decyzje i uruchamiać właściwe kompetencje w odpowiednim momencie.

Za co będziesz odpowiadać?

  • Business & Client Leadership – budowanie długoterminowych relacji z klientami, rozumienie ich biznesu i pełnienie roli strategicznego partnera, a nie wyłącznie dostawcy usług mediowych.

  • Strategic Direction – definiowanie wspólnie z klientem i zespołem kierunku działań, stawianie właściwych pytań oraz przekładanie danych, insightów i zmian rynkowych na rekomendacje biznesowe i mediowe.

  • Integrated Delivery – integracja pracy zespołów strategii, mediów, performance, data & analytics, technologii, e-commerce i innych kompetencji Group One wokół wspólnego celu klienta.

  • People Management – zarządzanie i rozwój zespołu, wyznaczanie kierunku, budowanie odpowiedzialności i samodzielności oraz tworzenie środowiska, w którym ludzie mogą podejmować decyzje w duchu lider to lider i rozwijać swoje kompetencje.

title: SR. QS
description:
Job Summary

To lead and manage project cost control, measurement, valuations, variations, and claims support to protect profitability and ensure accurate commercial reporting for large-scale construction operations.

Candidate Profile

Responsibilities

1) Pre-Contract & Tender Support (as assigned)

  • Review tender documents, BOQ, drawings, and specifications for commercial risks and opportunities.
  • Prepare quantity take-offs, pricing support, and clarification/exclusion notes.
  • Support subcontract tendering, evaluations, and commercial comparisons.

2) Cost Control & Budget Management

  • Establish and maintain project budget, cost breakdown structure, and cost-to-complete forecasts.
  • Monitor commitments, expenditures, and productivity impacts; issue monthly cost reports.
  • Support cashflow planning and payment prioritization aligned with project progress.

3) Measurement, Valuations & Payments

  • Prepare and certify interim valuations for client submissions and payment applications.
  • Measure works executed on site, reconcile quantities, and validate subcontractor claims.
  • Ensure timely preparation of subcontractor payment certificates and back-to-back compliance.

4) Variations & Change Management

  • Identify, quantify, and submit variations with proper substantiation (drawings, instructions, site records).
  • Maintain a Variation Register, track approvals, and update cost impact in forecasts.
  • Coordinate with PM/Planning for time and cost entitlement on changes.

5) Claims & Commercial Support

  • Support preparation of EOT and cost claims with contemporaneous records and programme analysis.
  • Maintain logs for notices, RFIs, instructions, and approvals to protect contractual entitlement.
  • Support negotiations and settlements with clients and subcontractors.

6) Subcontract & Procurement Commercial Control

  • Draft/review subcontract commercial terms (payments, retention, bonds, penalties, scope boundaries).
  • Manage subcontract final accounts and ensure correct closeout documentation.
  • Coordinate with Procurement to control rate changes, supplier terms, and delivery impacts.

7) Reporting, Governance & Compliance

  • Produce monthly commercial reports: cost vs budget, CVR, cashflow, variations, claims status, risks.
  • Ensure documentation is audit-ready and aligned with contract conditions (FIDIC knowledge preferred).
  • Provide commercial risk alerts to management with mitigation recommendations.


Skills

Qualification

Bachelor’s Degree in Quantity Surveying / Civil Engineering / Construction Management.

MRICS (or progress toward) is an advantage.

Measurement and BOQ management, interim valuations, and final accounts.

Strong knowledge of contracts (FIDIC/standard forms), variations, and claims basics.

Proficient in Excel and reporting; ERP/Cost control systems experience is a plus.

Required Experiences

  • 10–12+ years QS experience in UAE/GCC construction.
  • Strong exposure to large projects and complex subcontractor management.
  • Experience in Abu Dhabi client/consultant environments is preferred.

title: Policy Manager – Creative Industries and Festivals
description:
**This is an Expression of Interest (EOI) opportunity, available on a lateral move basis only. Applications are open to Core Scottish Government employees only.**

**Job Title** – Policy Manager – Creative Industries and Festivals

**Working Arrangement** – Staff in roles compatible with hybrid working should spend 40% of their contracted working time working in person at their contractual workplace. More information can be found within [Hybrid Working Policy](https://scotsconnect.sharepoint.com/sites/saltireredirect?siteId=mylifeandcareer&pageId=8c5a454f-11b6-4349-a97e-96ba6acf3f51&pageParams=working-in-person-hybrid-working) .

**Grade** – B3

**Advert type** – **level transfer**

**Duration** – Permanent

**Eligibility** - Expressions of interest are invited from substantive colleagues on level transfer from Core SG only.

**Skilled Worker Sponsorship not being offered**

Skilled Worker sponsorship is not available for this role. As a result, we are unable to appoint candidates who require Skilled Worker sponsorship now or in the future. Applicants must have an existing and ongoing right to work in the UK.

**Overview**

Creative Industries and Festivals represents some of the most important elements of culture that support the economy. The screen sector is forecast to reach £1bn GVA by 2030, creative industries has grown at four times the rate of the rest of the economy over the past decade, and the major Edinburgh festivals alone are forecast to deliver gross economic impact of more than £4.2 billion in Scotland over the next five years.

This Creative Industries and Festivals Unit leads the Scottish Government’s focus on this area, this includes policy development across screen and broadcasting, festivals policy and delivery, and creative industries workforce, as well as supporting the work undertaken directly by our public bodies such as Creative Scotland, Screen Scotland and Visit Scotland.

The unit is also responsible for the high profile delivery of manifesto and Programme for Government commitments. These include: setting up Screen Scotland as an independent body; the establishment of a Film and TV School; expansion of funding to enhance the ambitions of Scotland's arts festivals, and; the piloting of a minimum income for artists.

As a cross-cutting role, the post holder will build, develop and maintain strong relationships with partners across creative industries, screen, festivals as well as the broader culture sector and beyond, helping to support and enhance some of our country’s most significant national and international assets.

Working across these three areas will provide the post holder with an exciting array of both short-term focused projects, long-term policy development as well as leading on elements of Ministerial and stakeholder engagement.

The Culture and Historic Environment Division as a whole is responsible for: sponsoring culture public bodies and organisations such as Historic Environment Scotland, Creative Scotland and the national collection bodies; ensuring everyone can participate in and enjoy culture; and creating the conditions for creative people and businesses to thrive.

The key tasks and deliverables you may be responsible for include:

- Supporting the work to establish Screen Scotland as an independent public body, through the design, legislation, and delivery process;
- Supporting work to establish a new Television Festival in Edinburgh;
- Leading on early scoping work for the creation of a new Film and Television School;
- Support the development of work to strengthen the evidence base we draw on to develop policy to support Scotland’s arts festivals
- Lead and/or support ongoing work to address key barriers to the sustainability of Scotland’s arts festivals—such as accommodation, affordability, and infrastructure - collaborating across Scottish Government, public sector partners, local authorities and beyond.
- Management of the recently launched Expanded Festivals Fund, working closely with Creative Scotland, arts festivals and other partners to shape its future development.
- Provide concise, rigorous advice to senior colleagues and Ministers - working collaboratively and supporting the team in the production of accurate and high-quality written briefings, submissions, Parliamentary Questions, FOIs, and correspondence.
- Support Ministers and senior staff at meetings and engagements;
- Work flexibly across the Unit and Division as business requires, as well as being prepared to undertake activity as needed during peak periods such as related to major events like the annual programme of Edinburgh Festivals, signature events such Celtic Connections, Glasgow Film Festival and other arts festivals across Scotland.

**Success profile**

Success profiles are specific to each job and they include the mix of skills, experience and behaviours candidates will be assessed on. You can find out more about Success Profiles [here](https://www.gov.scot/publications/success-profiles-candidate-guide/pages/behaviour-levels/):

**Experience**

- Proven experience of working strategically and creatively across boundaries, developing thinking on cross-cutting policy areas;
- Experience in the legislative and/or Parliamentary process;
- Excellent communication skills, including an ability to develop trusted working relationships with internal and external stakeholders;
- A track record of strong organisational skills, preferably including project management skills;
- Good analytical skills, including the ability to work with analysts and to draw out key conclusions and policy implications.
- A good understanding of the workings of government and how it relates to the wider public and/or culture sector

**Technical Skills:**

1. Policy Context and Purpose – Level 2 - Practitioner
2. Participation and Engagement – Level 2 - Practitioner
3. Parliament and Law – Level 2 – Practitioner
4. Policy Delivery and Systems – Level 2 – Practitioner

You can find out more about the skills required, [here](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1065809/UPDATED_PP_Standards_annex_v6_acc.pdf)

**Behaviours:**

- Seeing the Big Picture – Level 3
- Changing and Improving – Level 3
- Making Effective Decisions – Level 3
- Working Together – Level 3

**Working Pattern**

The post is a full-time role, but staff with different working patterns are invited to apply, and we will assess proposed working patterns against the business requirements for this post.   This post is based in Victoria Quay with a mix of office-based and remote working.  The current team anchor day is Wednesday in VQ.

Our standard hours are 35 hours per week and we offer a range of flexible working options depending on the needs of the role, including Flexi-leave. Scottish Government staff in hybrid-compatible roles should work in-person 40% of the time, either in an office or other agreed work location. If you have specific questions about the role you are applying for, please contact us.

**How to Apply**

Please submit a CV and an Expression of Interest (maximum 500 words) outlining your suitability for the role, relevant skills and experience, and what you would bring to the team. Please align this to how you meet the behaviours, experience and technical skills listed in the Success Profile above.

Vacancies close at 11:59pm on the date displayed in the table, unless otherwise stated on the job advert.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools can be used to support your application, but all statements and examples provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, and presented as your own) applications will be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action.

Please see our [candidate guidance](https://www.gov.scot/publications/recruitment-candidate-guide/pages/use-of-ai-tools/) for more information on acceptable and unacceptable uses of AI in recruitment.

If invited for further assessment, this will consist of a light touch interview.

Discussions are to be confirmed.

For any questions relating to your expression of interest please contact Emily.Green@gov.scot

**Recruitment Principles**

As a government organisation, we adhere to the [Civil Service Commission Recruitment Principles](https://civilservicecommission.independent.gov.uk/document/02a-recruitment-principles-april-2018-final/?d102_cookies_enabled=all) and we investigate any complaints received in relation to recruitment cases.

**About us**

The Scottish Government is the devolved government for Scotland. We have responsibility for a wide range of key policy areas including: education, health, the economy, justice, housing and transport. We offer rewarding careers and employ people across Scotland in a wide range of professions and roles.

Our staff are part of the [UK Civil Service](https://www.civil-service-careers.gov.uk/about-us/) observing the Civil Service Codeand working for Ministers and senior stakeholders to deliver vital public services which improve the lives of the people of Scotland.

We offer a supportive and inclusive working environment along with a wide range of employee benefits. Find out more about [what we offer](https://www.jobs.gov.scot/what-we-offer).

As part of the UK Civil Service, we uphold the [Civil Service Nationality Rules](https://www.gov.scot/publications/recruitment-candidate-guide/pages/nationality-requirements/).

**Security checks**

Successful candidates must complete the Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS), before they can be appointed. BPSS is comprised of four main pre-employment checks – Identity, Right to work, Employment History and a Criminal Record check (unspent convictions).

You can find out more about BPSS on the [UK Government website](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-baseline-personnel-security-standard), or read about the different levels of security checks in our [Candidate Guide](https://www.gov.scot/publications/recruitment-candidate-guide/pages/pre-employment-checks/).

**Equality statement**

We are committed to equality and inclusion and we aim to recruit a diverse workforce that reflects the population of our nation.

Find out more about our commitment to [diversity](https://www.jobs.gov.scot/an-inclusive-organisation) and how we offer and support [recruitment adjustments](https://www.jobs.gov.scot/requesting-adjustments-2) for anyone who needs them.

**Further information**

Find out more about our organisation, what we offer staff members and how to apply on our [Careers Website](https://www.jobs.gov.scot/).

Read our [Candidate Guide](https://www.gov.scot/publications/recruitment-candidate-guide/pages/introduction/) for further information on our recruitment and application processes.

title: University Engagement Strategist
description:
**Organizational Background**

In the heart of the nation’s capital, George Washington University (GW) is the largest institution of higher education in the District of Columbia. The University offers comprehensive programs of undergraduate and graduate liberal arts study, as well as degree programs in medicine, public health, law, engineering, education, business, and international affairs. As one of the largest private employers in the District of Columbia, the University seeks employees who support the teaching, research, and public service mission of the University.

**Job Description Summary**

Reporting to the Executive Director, Talent Development, the University Engagement Strategist serves as a strategic lead and individual contributor responsible for designing, managing, and evaluating university-wide engagement programs, culture initiatives, and staff recognition for the George Washington University.

This position bridges data-driven culture strategy with high-impact execution. The University Engagement Strategist acts as the central HR lead for university culture, synthesizing employee feedback for executive leadership while partnering closely with University Events, HR Business Partners (HRBPs), University Communications, and institutional stakeholders to drive staff connection, appreciation, and community across campus and remote/hybrid work environments.

**Key Areas of Responsibility**

**1. Strategic Culture & Survey Management**

- Serve as the functional and strategic lead for the annual university-wide employee engagement survey, managing the vendor relationship, survey administration, communication strategies, and data integrity.
- Analyze complex survey data and synthesize findings into executive-level briefings, delivering actionable updates, trend analysis, and recommendations to Deans, Vice Presidents, and Cabinet leadership.
- Partner with HR Business Partners (HRBPs) and unit leaders to facilitate post-survey action planning, designing central toolkits, train-the-trainer resources, and tailored engagement strategies for decentralized units.
- Explore and implement ongoing employee feedback mechanisms (e.g., pulse surveys, lifecycle feedback) to continuously evaluate the employee experience.

**2. Staff Recognition and Community Events**

- Drive the strategy and program design for marquee university-wide staff appreciation initiatives, including the annual GW Step Challenge, employee socials, and community-building events.
- Serve as the primary HR lead in partnership with the University Events team to co-design and execute large-scale signature events (500–2000+ attendees), including the annual Employee Festival and Staff Awards.
- Direct the university’s Career Milestone program, managing vendor agreements, communications, the gift/yearbook platform, and the annual recognition ceremony.
- Oversee the annual review and administration of the Staff Emeriti program.

**3. Program Operations, Budgeting, & Strategic Communications**

- Manage the employee event, engagement budget, tracking expenditures and negotiating with external vendors to maximize program ROI.
- Partner with university communications and internal communication team to develop comprehensive messaging, branding, and promotional plans to increase awareness and participation in engagement initiatives.
- Maintain central engagement and leadership calendars to maximize visibility, participation, and alignment across all university initiatives.
- Establish metrics and analytics to evaluate the reach, participation rate, and overall impact of engagement programs across the university.
- Provide supervision or oversight to event-day support staff, student workers, or temporary staff as required.

Perform all other duties as assigned. The omission of specific duties does not preclude the supervisor from assigning duties that are logically related to the position.

title: Historic Places Regeneration Officer
description:
**Summary**

Historic England is the public organisation that brings new life to heritage to build a better future for every place and everyone.

Historic England has a fantastic opportunity for you to join us as our Historic Places Regeneration Officer.

**This is a part time (28.8 hours per week), this is a fixed term contract until end of March 2028.**

The location of this role is Manchester, Newcastle or York, inclusive with hybrid working.

We offer a wide benefits package including a competitive defined benefit **pension scheme to which we make 28.97% employer contributions,** a generous 28 days holiday, corporate discounts, free entry into English Heritage sites across the country and development opportunities to ensure you achieve your goals.

To view our full range of benefits please follow the link [here](https://historicengland.org.uk/about/jobs/employee-rewards-and-benefits/).

**What you will be doing**

The Historic Places Regeneration Officer will support delivery of our programme for priority places, working closely with the Historic Places Regeneration Advisers and other colleagues in the Historic Places Regeneration Team.  Regeneration Officers will draw on their skills, whether project management, archaeological, urban design, community engagement, etc., to deliver exemplary and impactful projects.

Regeneration Officers make full use of Historic England’s breath of expertise and tools, including grants (both Historic England and Defra funded) and the heritage at risk programme, and they work with external partners to transform the heritage that matters to communities through heritage led regeneration.

**Who we are looking for**

- Experience of assessing, managing, delivering grant funded projects

- Experience of working with grassroots / community organisations

- Ability to solve problems and work creatively to achieve results

- Ability to advocate for the value of heritage in place based regeneration

- Experience of partnership working


**Please note your application will be scored and assessed against the above criteria.**

Historic England is a Disability Confident Leader and normally offers guaranteed interviews to disabled candidates who meet the minimum criteria for the role, where it is practical and appropriate to do so. We want all candidates to shine in the recruitment process, so please tell us what we can do to help you show us your very best self. For more information, please visit our [Everyone is Welcome page](https://historicengland.org.uk/about/jobs/everyone-is-welcome/ "https://historicengland.org.uk/about/jobs/everyone-is-welcome/"), or contact us at [recruitmentTeam@Historicengland.org.uk](mailto:recruitmentTeam@Historicengland.org.uk) if you have any recruitment queries.

We are an equal opportunity employer which values diversity and inclusion. If you have a disability or neurodiversity, we would be happy to discuss reasonable adjustments to the job with you. Having won the Gold Award from MIND for workplace wellbeing in seven consecutive years, we also recognise the importance of a healthy work-life balance.

We are an inclusive employer and believe that flexible working options are for everyone. We want to make sure our working arrangements don’t prevent anyone from joining us because of their personal circumstances. We also want to provide you with the best balance in your home and work life that we can.

We are open to considering options including job sharing, part-time working, compressed hours working and different working locations, including hybrid working. Please visit our jobs pages or contact us to find out more.

**Why work for Historic England**

We are committed to promoting equality of opportunity for everyone. Diversity helps us to perform better and attract more people to support our work. We welcome and encourage job applications from people of all backgrounds.

We particularly encourage applications from Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic candidates and candidates with disabilities as they are underrepresented within Historic England at this level.

Historic England wants all of our candidates to shine in the recruitment process. Please tell us what we can do to make sure you can show us your very best self. You can contact us by email at [recruitmentTeam@Historicengland.org.uk](mailto:recruitmentTeam@Historicengland.org.uk) if you have any recruitment queries.

**At Historic England we use a hiring system called Applied. Applied is a behavioural science-backed recruitment platform that reduces bias, improves quality of hire and increases diversity. We do not use CV application for the majority of our hiring processes. You will answer a selection of questions that allow our hiring teams to test your skills and suitability for the role.**

At Historic England, we value the expertise and individuality each candidate brings and want to hear about this in your own words. If you require the use or AI tools or other resources to support your application, we ask that all information is factually accurate, original, and reflects your own experience. To best represent yourself, we encourage you to write in your own words and use AI-generated content only as inspiration—not as direct input.

Provisional interview dates: 8th and 15th December 2026

Please follow the link for a full copy of the Job Description –

[https://historicengland.org.uk/media/yufnhuhh/zw-historic-places-regeneration-officer-north-jd-oct-26.odt](https://cms.historicengland.org.uk/media/yufnhuhh/zw-historic-places-regeneration-officer-north-jd-oct-26.odt)

**Historic England only accepts applications through our authorised recruitment platform, Applied. We will never ask applicants to pay any fee or provide payment details during the recruitment process. Please only apply using the application link provided within this advert.**

  • sprawne załatwienie formalności związanych z zatrudnieniem

title: Privacy Systems Analyst
description:
Who we are: 
At Rover, pets and their people are at the heart of everything we do. We connect pet parents with trusted pet care across the U.S., Canada, Europe, and Australia.
Headquartered in Seattle and Barcelona, we’re a values driven, fast-growing tech company focused on building safe and personalized experiences tailored to the needs of each unique pet. We’re investing in AI as a business accelerator and provide every team member access to AI tools in service of creating better experiences for our community.
We are proud to be recognized as a great place to work, having been named among the 100 Best Companies to Work For in Seattle Business Magazine and Washington’s Best Workplaces in the Puget Sound Business Journal. At Rover we’re committed to creating an accessible, inclusive, and welcoming community, which starts with our employees.
Want to make an impact? Join our pack and come work (and play!) with us.


About the Role
We're looking for a hands-on, technically driven Privacy Systems Analyst to own Rover's privacy technology platform stack. You'll be the technical operator behind our privacy compliance program: configuring, integrating, troubleshooting, and maintaining our privacy management platform and the systems connected to it.
You'll partner closely with the GRC team, who own the program-level requirements, and make sure what compliance defines, the platform reliably delivers. We're especially looking for someone with a strong instinct for automating manual work, including with AI tooling, and the technical depth to keep the privacy stack performing at scale.
 This is a hybrid position that has the minimum expectation to work out of our Barcelona Office in the Poblenou neighborhood two days per week on Mondays and Thursdays. For this reason, candidates must be based in Barcelona or willing to relocate.

What You'll Do:
Own the privacy platform: configure and maintain workflows, assessments, consent management, DSAR automation, and reporting. Be the go-to person when something isn't working.
Coordinate consent and marketing preferences: support opt-in/opt-out workflows with Marketing, Legal, and Engineering; ensure preference signals are captured, synced, and enforced correctly downstream; troubleshoot gaps between what's configured and what's actually enforced.
Manage integrations and APIs: own the API surface connecting the privacy platform to other Rover systems, including authentication, error handling, and monitoring.
Handle DSARs end to end: ensure connectors fire correctly, monitor success rates, and resolve errors that block fulfillment.
Keep RoPA and Data Map accurate: maintain connectors, validate data inventory, and onboard new sources.
Lead new integrations: act as technical lead on integration projects, from design through go-live.
Support incident response: partner with Cybersecurity on privacy/security incidents, owning platform-level triage and technical evidence collection.
Build AI-driven automation: identify manual, repetitive work (DSAR intake, RoPA upkeep, documentation, vendor tickets) and build AI-assisted workflows to reduce it, always with human review for compliance-sensitive output.
Document and mentor: keep configurations, runbooks, and troubleshooting guides current; support more junior team members.
Own the vendor relationship: raise and manage technical escalations with evidence, and engage vendor professional services only when the work genuinely exceeds in-house capability.

What You'll Need:
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or equivalent practical experience
2-5 years administering SaaS platforms, with experience leading moderately complex projects
Hands-on experience with an enterprise privacy management platform (consent management, DSAR automation, data discovery)
Working knowledge of REST APIs, OAuth/API keys, webhooks, and integration troubleshooting
Understanding of SaaS architecture: environments, sandbox-to-production, change management
Strong independent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills
Clear communication, especially with non-technical stakeholders
Comfortable working autonomously and knowing when to escalate
Practical, hands-on experience using AI/LLM tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) to automate workflows, draft documentation, or accelerate troubleshooting

Nice to Have:
Vendor certifications (OneTrust, Ketch, DataGrail, TrustArc, or similar)
Cloud fundamentals certifications (AWS, Azure, GCP)
GDPR/CCPA or global privacy regulation awareness
Scripting experience (Python, JavaScript)
IAM/SSO knowledge
Experience with AI coding tools (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor) or calling LLM APIs directly
Awareness of AI governance frameworks (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001)

Benefits of Working at Rover.com:
Long-term incentive plan with a company performance-based cash payout
Pension plan
Private medical insurance
25 days PTO
Meal allowance and flexible compensation plan (transport and nursery)
Gym membership
€450 to cover the costs associated with the adoption of a pet
Annual €150 wellness reimbursement
Flexible work hours, sometimes you'll need to be in at certain times, but on the whole, we're pretty flexible when it comes to managing workload and time
Grab snacks, fresh fruit, in our kitchen to keep yourself going
Regular team activities, events, game nights, and more
Dog-friendly office

Compensation:
In the greater Barcelona area the first-year salary range is €38,946 - €47,207. Additionally, Rover offers a long-term incentive plan with a company performance-based cash payout and benefits to full-time employees.
The cash compensation offered for this role will be dependent on the candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, and abilities as demonstrated in the interview and hiring process.

Rover is an equal-opportunity employer committed to promoting a diverse, inclusive, and inventive environment with the best employees. We’re driven by seeing our people succeed and grow, and we work to ensure everyone contributes to their fullest potential. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to age, race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, disability, protected veteran status, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or any other protected status in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances.

title: Estimation Engineer - Electrical
description:
Job Summary

We are seeking an experienced Electrical Estimation Engineer with a strong background in MEP contracting to handle electrical estimation, tender preparation, cost analysis, and preparation of competitive project quotations. The candidate should have hands-on experience in reviewing tender documents, preparing BOQs, evaluating project costs, and coordinating with suppliers and subcontractors.


Key Responsibilities


  • Review tender documents, drawings, specifications, BOQs, and scope of work to understand project requirements.
  • Prepare detailed electrical cost estimates for MEP projects, including material, labour, equipment, and installation costs.
  • Conduct quantity take-offs from electrical drawings and specifications.
  • Prepare and review Bill of Quantities (BOQ) and detailed cost breakdowns.
  • Estimate costs for electrical systems, including:
  • Power distribution systems, LV panels and switchgear.
  • Lighting and lighting control systems.
  • Cable trays, trunking, conduits and wiring.
  • Power and lighting installations.
  • Earthing and lightning protection systems.
  • Fire alarm and emergency lighting systems.
  • ELV systems, including CCTV, access control, structured cabling and public address systems.
  • Electrical equipment and associated installations.
  • Obtain and evaluate quotations from suppliers and subcontractors.
  • Prepare technical and commercial tender submissions in accordance with project requirements.
  • Analyse material and labour costs and identify cost-saving opportunities.
  • Coordinate with the procurement, engineering, project and tendering teams to ensure accurate estimates.
  • Prepare tender clarifications, technical queries and commercial comparisons.
  • Maintain and update cost databases, supplier rates and estimation records.
  • Assist in preparing tender proposals, cost summaries and final submission documents.


Skills

Educational Qualifications


  • Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent.
  • Relevant professional experience in electrical estimation within MEP contracting companies.

Required Skills & Experience


  • Minimum 5–8 years of experience in electrical estimation and tendering within MEP contracting companies.
  • Strong knowledge of electrical systems, materials, installation methods and applicable standards.
  • Hands-on experience in quantity take-offs and BOQ preparation.
  • Ability to interpret electrical drawings, specifications and tender documents.
  • Proficiency in AutoCAD, Microsoft Excel and electrical estimation software.
  • Experience in supplier and subcontractor quotation evaluation.
  • Strong analytical, commercial and cost-control skills.
  • Ability to work independently and meet tight tender submission deadlines.
  • Good communication, coordination and negotiation skills.

Preferred Experience


  • Experience in handling large-scale commercial, residential, industrial and government MEP projects.
  • Familiarity with Kuwait market rates, suppliers and subcontractors.
  • Previous experience in preparing competitive tenders for MEP contracting projects.

title: Deputy Solicitor
description:
Be part of a statutory public inquiry to keep children safer in the future.

The **Deputy Solicitor** to the Inquiry will play a leadership role in the Inquiry investigations team, working closely with the Solicitor to the Inquiry in investigating the evidence, identifying witnesses, managing the oral hearings, contributing to drafting of the interim reports and assisting in meeting the publication process deadlines. The overall Inquiry investigations team will work flexibly and constructively with Counsel to the Inquiry and all other teams to ensure the efficient delivery of outcomes and support for the Chair.

The Jay Inquiry is a statutory public inquiry set up under the Inquiries Act 2005 to investigate group based sexual abuse and exploitation of children in Scotland, examine institutional responses to it and make recommendations to better protect children both now and in the future. The inquiry is independent of Scottish Ministers, meaning that the direction and functioning of the inquiry is for its Chair.

When announcing the setting up of the inquiry in early 2026, the Cabinet Secretary for Education stated that “survivors of abuse want to see accountability and improvement delivered as quickly as possible, and that sense of urgency is shared by the Scottish Government. We are determined to act decisively to protect children from the horrendous harm of child sexual abuse and exploitation.

The terms of reference are intentionally broad in nature following discussions with survivors and survivor groups and in order to allow the Chair, Professor Alexis Jay, to set out lines of enquiry that best fulfil the remit. In determining those lines of enquiry, the Chair wishes to hear from survivors.

**The Inquiry aims to uphold the highest standards of independence and impartiality. Before applying, all candidates are asked to consider if their career history gives rise to any conflict of interest with the Inquiry’s Terms of Reference.**

**Responsibilities**

- Provide legal advice to the Chair and the Inquiry team, particularly in relation to the application of the Inquiries Act 2005, the Inquiries (Scotland) Rules 2007, and data handling requirements, including data protection matters.
- Instruct and liaise with Counsel to the Inquiry to identify lines of inquiry to be pursued by the Investigations Team.
- Draft the Inquiry's procedure and protocol documents, monitoring and ensuring compliance with them.
- Work closely with the Delivery & Assurance Programme Team to develop plans and witness trackers that support oral hearing delivery timescales.
- Work closely with the Records & Evidence Team to ensure that the Inquiry record complies with data protection legislation and is appropriately prepared for transfer to the National Records of Scotland.
- Liaise with solicitors representing Core Participants.
- As a member of the leadership team, contribute to a positive working environment that supports diversity, equality, and health and wellbeing.
- Work with other teams to identify, manage, and review evidence and documents submitted to the Inquiry.
- Lead the recruitment and line management of Assistant Solicitors and other legal team members, providing resilience, motivation and support to develop individuals and teams, manage change, and meet challenging deadlines and competing priorities.

**Qualifications**

- The Deputy Solicitor to the Inquiry must be a solicitor or advocate entitled to practise in Scotland and hold a current Practising Certificate.
- Applications from Solicitors qualified in other jurisdictions may be considered where they can clearly demonstrate they meet the essential and desirable criteria.


Proof of qualifications will be checked at the assessment stage.

**Success profile**

Success profiles are specific to each job and they include the mix of behaviours, experience and technical criteria (if applicable) that candidates will be assessed on.

**Experience**

- A strong track record of providing high-quality legal advice to agreed deadlines with competing priorities.


**Desirable Criteria**

- Experience of working with vulnerable individuals and an understanding of using trauma informed approaches.
- Litigation or Inquiry experience within Scotland.


_Desirable criteria will only be used in the event of a strong field of candidates, and as a second stage after Experience and Behaviours have been considered._

**Behaviours**

1. Seeing the bigger picture - Level 4
2. Delivering at pace - Level 4
3. Making effective decisions - Level 4
4. Working together - Level 4
5. Leadership - Level 4


Find out more about Success Profiles.

**How to apply**

Apply online, providing a CV and supporting statement (of no more than 1500 words) providing evidence of how you meet the behaviours, experience and technical skills listed in the Success Profile above. Both the CV and the supporting statement provided will be assessed against the criteria for the role.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools can be used to support your application, but all statements and examples provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, and presented as your own) applications will be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action.

Please see our candidate guidance for more information on acceptable and unacceptable uses of AI in recruitment.

**Skilled Worker Sponsorship not being offered**

Skilled Worker sponsorship is not available for this role. As a result, we are unable to appoint candidates who require Skilled Worker sponsorship now or in the future. Applicants must have an existing and ongoing right to work in the UK.

If invited for further assessment, this will consist of an interview and **presentation.**

Assessments are scheduled for w/c 7th December 2026however this may be subject to change.

**Apply before 23:59 on 23rd November 2026. This post is open to internal candidates and Common Citizenship Organisations only (external candidates and staff from UK Other Government Departments are not eligible to apply for this vacancy).**

**Recruitment Principles**

As a government organisation, we adhere to the Civil Service Commission Recruitment Principles and we investigate any complaints received in relation to recruitment cases.

**About us**

The Scottish Government is the devolved government for Scotland. We have responsibility for a wide range of key policy areas including: education, health, the economy, justice, housing and transport. We offer rewarding careers and employ people across Scotland in a wide range of professions and roles.

Our staff are part of the UK Civil Service, observing the Civil Service Code and working for Ministers and senior stakeholders to deliver vital public services which improve the lives of the people of Scotland.

We offer a supportive and inclusive working environment along with a wide range of employee benefits. Find out more about what we offer.

As part of the UK Civil Service, we uphold the Civil Service Nationality Rules.

**Working pattern**

This post is a full-time role (35 hours) with the expectation that at least 40% of the working week will be spent in the Inquiry offices in central Edinburgh. Due to the nature of delivery within a public Inquiry there will be times when individuals are required to attend the office on a more regular basis.

We encourage applications from individuals on a variety of working patterns and offer a range of flexible working options depending on the needs of the role.

**Minimum Time in Post**

There is an expectation that the successful applicant will stay in post for the duration of the Inquiry. Whilst there is no set timescale for the Inquiry, applicants should be aware that Inquiries can last typically 5+ years.

**Security checks**

Successful candidates must complete the Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS), before they can be appointed. BPSS is comprised of four main pre-employment checks – Identity, Right to work, Employment History and a Criminal Record check (unspent convictions).

You can find out more about BPSS on the UK Government website, and read about the Government Vetting Charter, or about all the different levels of security checks in our Candidate Guide.

Candidates may need to gain higher security clearance than they currently hold if successful in their application which may include a PVG check.

**Equality statement**

We are committed to equality and inclusion and we aim to recruit a diverse workforce that reflects the population of our nation.

Find out more about our commitment to diversity and how we offer and support recruitment adjustments for anyone who needs them.

**Further information**

Find out more about our organisation, what we offer staff members and how to apply on our Careers Website.

Read our Candidate Guide for further information on our recruitment and application processes.

Daymark Health is backed by Maverick Ventures, Yosemite, Oncology Ventures, Healthier Capital, Blue Venture Fund, and Healthcare Foundry.

Be cautious of recruitment fraud, and always confirm that communications are coming from an official Daymark Health email.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Health Partners are core members of the Daymark care team, supporting integrated, whole-person care for our patients. In this role, you will coordinate social and logistical aspects of care, spending time connecting with patients and caregivers by phone, video, and occasionally in the home. You will help patients navigate community-based and social services, ensure follow-up appointments are scheduled, and support seamless coordination between Daymark and external providers.

This is a fast-paced, high-accountability environment. Success requires strong prioritization, attention to detail, and the ability to deliver high-quality work at speed.

Note: This is a full time position required to be onsite 5 days a week in The Long Beach, CA office.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Conduct structured social needs assessments (SDOH) and connect patients with community resources, which may include transportation, financial assistance, food, medical equipment, or emotional support programs.
  • Support development of patients’ care plans and participate in case conferences to ensure quality care delivery.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for virtual visit readiness and basic technology troubleshooting.
  • Coordinate and schedule care for patients, including scheduling follow-up visits and facilitating referrals.
  • Own structured chart preparation to ensure providers are visit-ready, including accurate contact, insurance, and care team information.
  • Track completion of our Symptom Survey, complete all appropriate follow ups, and escalate clinical concerns as needed.
  • Document social interventions, tasks, and care coordination activities in the electronic health record in a timely and standardized format.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

  • Experience. You have at least 3 years of experience in healthcare navigation or patient support, or related experience in a clinical or care coordination setting.
  • Comfort with Technology. You’re comfortable using Slack, Zoom, the Google Suite, and EHR systems to ensure accurate appointment scheduling and management and support patients virtually.
  • Bias to action: You don’t wait for someone to tell you what to do. You know how to identify and prioritize your initiative’s needs and you do what it takes to ensure that urgent and important needs are acted on immediately.
  • Comfort with change and ambiguity: You may not always have direction in your work, and that’s OK, because you’re comfortable figuring out what needs to be done and a path forward.
  • Strong relational skills. You have an uncanny ability to establish rapport and work effectively with diverse populations including health care providers, clinical staff, patients, and family members.
  • Organized & Communicative. You are incredibly organized and sweat the details. You keep your team in the loop with what you’re working on and the challenges you’re facing and are proficient in collecting patient clinical and demographic data and documenting appropriately in a timely manner.
  • Open to working from Daymark's local office: You're comfortable working out of our office in Providence, Rhode Island 5 days of the week, and occasionally, visiting patient's homes.
  • Bilingual: is a plus but is not required.

Compensation Range: $55,000 - $60,000 USD
Location: Fully onsite (5 days a week) in Long Beach, CA; 8:30am - 5:00pm.

title: Director, Product Management, Provider Experience
description:
Who we are: 
At Rover, pets and their people are at the heart of everything we do. We connect pet parents with trusted pet care across the U.S., Canada, Europe, and Australia.
Headquartered in Seattle and Barcelona, we’re a values driven, fast-growing tech company focused on building safe and personalized experiences tailored to the needs of each unique pet. We’re investing in AI as a business accelerator and provide every team member access to AI tools in service of creating better experiences for our community.
We are proud to be recognized as a great place to work, having been named among the 100 Best Companies to Work For in Seattle Business Magazine and Washington’s Best Workplaces in the Puget Sound Business Journal. At Rover we’re committed to creating an accessible, inclusive, and welcoming community, which starts with our employees.
Want to make an impact? Join our pack and come work (and play!) with us.


About the role
Rover is looking for a Director of Product Management to lead the Provider Product Group inside our Global Provider Organization. In this role, you will own the product strategy and execution of Rover's multi-year provider roadmap: concentrating investment on our most successful providers while engaging our broader community of caregivers to strengthen marketplace depth and develop a high quality pipeline. 
You will lead four product teams working in service to our care providers, improving their experience and how they interact with the marketplace at every stage of their journey. This is a high-impact role that requires a unique blend of strategic vision and detailed-oriented, hands-on execution. You will set multi-year product direction and drive rigorous, experiment-led execution. The role carries direct accountability for supply-side revenue, provider retention, and new-customer booking growth.
This role reports directly to the Senior Director of Supply based in Barcelona, and partners closely with Data Science, Engineering, Design, Trust & Safety, Marketing, Operations, Finance, Legal, and the International Business Team.
As a people leader, you will manage a team of product managers based primarily in Barcelona and coordinate with cross-functional teams across Europe and the US.

* This is a hybrid position that has the minimum expectation to work out of our Barcelona Office in the Poblenou neighborhood two days per week on Mondays and Thursdays. For this reason, candidates must be based in Barcelona or willing to relocate.

What you'll own
Execution is delivered hand-in-hand with cross-functional partners; your job is to define the vision and what good looks like, sequence the bets, hold the alignment, and make sure all investments reinforce each other through excellent execution. 

Product Strategy and Vision. Own the multi-year provider product vision: translating Rover's provider strategy into a sequenced product direction and owning the narrative that aligns leadership, product teams, and partners behind it.
Roadmap and execution. Own the product side of the organization's OKRs and the roadmap that delivers them. Ship a steady cadence of well-crafted, experiment-validated launches, landed with quality and followed through after launch until the customer outcome is proven or the outcome is learned.
The voice of the provider. You will be the advocate for what providers actually want and need to grow and run top quality businesses, grounding every roadmap decision in customer research, feedback, and marketplace data, and representing that voice credibly in every executive conversation, including when it's inconvenient.
AI adoption. AI embedded in product features such as assisted tooling, intelligent messaging, personalization and education, as well as fostering AI in how the team works (AI-accelerated discovery, prototyping, execution), while building a culture of AI-native development as the default.
Cross-functional leadership. Hold alignment across Core Product Teams, Design, Engineering, Data Science, Marketing, Operations, Finance, Legal and Trust & Safety, and across regions, so that product investments reinforce each other globally rather than fragmenting by service, brand or country.
A team that sets the bar. Hire, coach and grow a team of product managers who combine judgment, customer centricity, inspiring craft and speed.

Minimum qualifications
10+ years of product management experience, with meaningful time in marketplace, platform, or two-sided business contexts. Experience in the supply-side of the marketplace is a plus.
5+ years in people management or leadership roles, including managing senior product managers or leading cross-functional groups.
Experience driving marketplace monetization — pricing, fee, or take-rate models — including designing, testing, and scaling pricing changes with measurable P&L impact.
Track record of building retention, engagement, and loyalty strategies for a professional user segment (providers, sellers, hosts, drivers, or merchants).Experience partnering with Data Science and Engineering teams to create and execute on shared roadmaps and metrics, with rigorous experimentation practice (A/B frameworks, holdouts, long-horizon measurement).
Clear and structured written and verbal communication style, with the ability to influence and partner with senior leaders and diverse teams to drive critical decisions.
Highly proactive, comfortable operating with minimal guidance in uncertain and ambiguous business environments.
Analytical rigour, with enthusiasm for modeling and measuring the impact of the initiatives you drive. Comfortable working with advanced analytical and visualization tools, such as Mode and Excel.
Strong leadership skills and experience giving actionable feedback and coaching, and welcoming the same.
Comfortable working across Europe (Central Time) and US (Pacific Time) timezones.
Strong command of the English language (minimum C2 level). English is the official Rover language and is used every day with every stakeholder and communication.Bachelor's degree.

Preferred qualifications
Experience in online marketplaces with a meaningful supply side (gig economy, services marketplaces, accommodation, mobility, creator platforms, or similar).
Experience with marketplace integrity problems: disintermediation and off-platform leakage, and incentive design that rewards loyal behavior.
Experience building customer-centric tooling, business-management software, or 'operating system' products for independent entrepreneurs.
Demonstrated success leading both 0-to-1 product bets and scaling existing product lines; comfort presenting to C-level and Board audiences.
Master's degree.

Competitive compensation

Pension Plan
Meal tickets through Cobee
25 days paid time off, plus public holidays
Private health insurance

Bring your dog to work (and unlimited puppy time)
Monetary help for adopting a dog plus yearly credit to use on our platform
Flexible work hours. We trust you to get your work done, and are not watching what times you're coming and going
Snacks and fresh fruit in our kitchen to keep yourself going
Regular team activities, including happy hours, game nights, and more
